item.title: Can Moscow and Seoul help Vietnam achieve its nuclear energy ambitions?
item.description: Vietnam has grand plans to build a series of nuclear power plants. But it faces several challenges.

item.title: Trump and Southeast Asia: When transactionalism undermines trust
item.description: The Trump Administration has broken with the tradition of pursuing its national interests in tandem with an emphasis on alliances and values. Southeast Asian countries will respond accordingly.

item.title: Sanae Takaichi supermajority opens path to nuclear-led, industry-driven energy transition in Japan
item.description: Landslide election win strengthens push to link decarbonisation with economic security, boosting nuclear, domestic clean tech and state-led industrial strategy while keeping climate targets intact.

item.title: Thirsty tech: Why chips and data centres are a growing water risk for investors
item.description: The Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) has published a new case study examining the financial risks that semiconductor and data centre firms could face due to their dependencies on water and ecosystem services.

item.title: Philippine energy department lauded for clampdown on non-performing renewable energy contracts
item.description: The department of energy has terminated agreements for nearly 18 gigawatts of solar, wind and other clean power projects due to prospective investors who were found to have no intention to build them.

item.title: What can China learn from California’s coal power exit?
item.description: With the right policy, coal is not essential to ensuring a reliable electricity supply.

item.title: Life returns to a damaged seagrass meadow in Malaysia
item.description: Seagrass restoration is increasingly recognised as crucial for addressing the twin crises of biodiversity loss and climate change.

item.title: Inside Singapore’s fish port, where experts say traceability gaps risk endangered species
item.description: Without traceability in the fisheries supply chain into Singapore, the catch traded at Jurong Fishery Port cannot be labelled "sustainable", say conservationists.

item.title: G7 ‘falling behind’ China as world’s wind and solar plans reach new high in 2025
item.description: The G7 major economies “f[e]ll notably behind China and the rest of the world” in 2025 as the amount of wind and solar power being developed reached a new high, according to Global Energy Monitor (GEM).

item.title: Southeast Asia can tap bond markets, improve taxonomies to fill adaptation finance gap: report
